title: PRAY PSALM 35 EVERY MORNING WHEN ENEMIES ARE RISING AGAINST YOU WATCH GOD RESPOND
text: There is a battle going on over your life, right now. Not tomorrow, not in some distant future. Right [music] now. And the reason you have not been sleeping, the reason the same obstacle keeps appearing in different clothing, the reason good things keep getting close and then something pulls them back, the reason you feel like you are pushing against an invisible wall, is because there are enemies. I did not say that to frighten you. I said it to prepare you because the first step to defeating an enemy is acknowledging that the enemy exists. And today, the spirit of God has summoned you to a war room. Not a sanctuary of retreat, a war room. And the weapon he has placed in your hands is Psalm 35. Before we go one step further, this is the most urgent instruction I will give you today. Share this word now. Before the prayer starts, >> [music] >> I'm not asking you to share a link. I am asking you to extend a lifeline. There is someone in your circle who is surrounded. Enemies on every side, accusations flying, character being assassinated, opportunities being sabotaged, and they do not know there is a Psalm, a legal apostolic blood-backed Psalm that David prayed when he was in exactly the same position, and God answered. Share this word as an act of warfare on behalf of someone else. That act of obedience will open a door for your own breakthrough because when you fight for others, God fights for you. Now, settle. Settle your spirit. Take a breath because I want to take you somewhere you have probably never been taken in this Psalm. Most believers know Psalm 35 exists. Very few have understood what it actually is. Psalm 35 is a lawsuit. Read that again. It It lawsuit. It is a legal petition >> [music] >> filed by David in the court of heaven. It is a man who understood that the battle he was facing was not just physical, it was judicial. It was a spiritual legal case that needed to be adjudicated by the judge of all the earth. David does not just cry out in Psalm 35, he files a case. He presents evidence, he names the charges, he calls the judge to act, he invokes covenant, he appeals to the righteousness of the court, and he waits for the verdict. There are dimensions to this that the average believer has never accessed. Most people pray Psalm 35 as [music] a desperate cry, but David prayed it as a legal argument. And when you understand the difference, you stop praying as a victim and start praying as a son presenting his case before his father, who also happens to be the supreme judge. Psalm 35 verse 1 through 3. Plead my cause, oh Lord, with them that strive with me. Fight against them that fight against me. Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help. Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me. Say unto my soul, I am thy salvation. Plead my cause. David's first word to God is not help me fight. It is plead my cause. He's appealing [music] [singing] to the legal function of God. He's saying, I am bringing this before the court. I am bringing [music] the case against me before the judge who knows the truth. Isaiah chapter 54 verse 17. No weapon formed against thee shall prosper, and [music] every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment, thou shalt condemn. Every tongue that rises in judgment, this is courtroom language. The enemy files charges, he [music] makes accusations, he presents false evidence. He's called the accuser of the brethren, Revelation 12:10 for a reason. He goes before the throne of God and he accuses. But here is what most believers do not know. You have a lawyer in that court. 1 John 2:2:1, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, an advocate, a legal representative, a counselor who stands before the judge on your behalf and the blood he presents as evidence cannot be overruled. When you pray Psalm 35, you are not just crying into the air. You are filing a brief in the court of heaven. You are saying judge of all the earth, I am bringing this case to you. These enemies have risen against me without cause. These accusations are false. These attacks are unjust and I am asking the court to rule in my favor and the court does not rule on feelings. The [music] court rules on covenant. And you have the blood of Jesus as your covenant document. [music] The case is already won before it is heard. Now go to verse 4 through 6. [music] Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul. Let them be turned back and brought to confusion that device my heart. Let them be as chaff before the wind and let the angel of the Lord chase them. Let their way be dark and slippery and let the angel of the Lord persecute them. Hear me, this is not theology. This is encounter. David is not being vindictive here. He's being precise. >> [music] >> He's decreeing not out of hatred but out of a righteous demand for justice. Let them be as chaff before the wind. Chaff has no weight. Chaff cannot stand against a breath. The things that have seemed so powerful against you, the enemy's plans, the enemies' conspiracies, the enemies' coordinated attacks in the presence of the wind of God, they are weightless. And notice, it is the angel of the Lord that chases them. David is not asking God to give him strength to chase his enemies. He's asking God to send his angel to do the chasing. This is the wisdom of the man who knows he does not need to fight [music] every battle personally. Some battles are too spiritual for human hands. [music] Some enemies are too powerful for natural weapons. But no enemy is too powerful for the angel of the Lord. 2 Chronicles chapter 32 verse 21. God sent an angel who cut off every mighty man of valor in the camp of the Assyrians. One angel, the entire army destroyed overnight. >> [music] >> While God's people slept, the spirit of God is saying something right now. He's saying, you have been trying to fight this battle with human strategy. You have been trying to outmaneuver the enemy with your intellect. You have been trying to defend yourself with your words and your connections and your effort, but this battle is not going to be won by your strategy. It is going to be won by the angel of the Lord. And the angel of the Lord moves when you pray. [music] Thus saith the spirit of God. The enemies who have been pursuing you are about to become the pursued. The one who was running from the attack is about to watch the attack reverse direction. The hunter becomes the hunted. [music] The accuser becomes the accused because the angel of the Lord has received his assignment. Let him fall into that very destruction. Without cause. This phrase appears twice in two verses. It is not accidental. David is establishing the injustice of the attack. He is saying to the judge, "These enemies have no legal ground. I did not provoke this. >> [music] >> I did not initiate this. They came after me without cause, and a judge who rules justly must respond differently to an unprovoked attack than to a provoked one. This matters for your prayer. This persecution is without cause. You are stepping aside and letting the one who has never lost a battle take the field. All my bones shall say, who is like unto thee? This is total body worship, not just the mouth, the bones. Every part of the physical structure giving praise because the victory is so complete, so overwhelming, so undeniably God >> [music] >> that the physical body cannot stay silent. But David in the middle of the attack, in the middle of the lawsuit, in the middle of the pressure, he lifts praise. Because praise is not a response to victory. It is a weapon that produces victory. [music] And suddenly an earthquake, doors opened, bands loosed, the praise broke open the prison. The one you prayed for. The one you defended. The one you invested in. John chapter 13 verse 18. Jesus quoted Psalm 41 verse 9.
